title: Discrete dynamic survival analysis of epidemic case line lists
abstract: Case line lists, which record dates of onset, recovery, and hospitalisation, are among the most granular data in infectious disease epidemiology and can provide insights into transmission dynamics. Dynamic survival analysis (DSA) fits a deterministic, differential-equation-based model to line lists to estimate parameters such as infectivity and the infectious period. Infectious periods are usually not exponential, and incorporating this into mechanistic models for line-list data often requires partial differential equation (PDE) schemes that can be difficult to implement and must be customised for each model, which may limit their use. Here, we propose Discrete Dynamic Survival Analysis (DDSA), a discrete-time DSA for case line lists based on difference equations. It matches calendar-day data directly without interpolation, and its log-likelihood is differentiable via forward-mode automatic differentiation, enabling off-the-shelf gradient-based samplers without model-specific numerical infrastructure. Non-exponential infectious periods are accommodated through a boxcar model or a discrete analogue of the "device of stages". We apply the DDSA method to three historical outbreaks of influenza A(H1N1), Ebola, and measles. DDSA estimates of transmission parameters were close to published analyses where these were available, an agreement that partly reflects shared modelling choices, and the method handles incomplete line lists with missing onset or recovery dates. Synthetic experiments show that recovery intervals identify the infectious period, while infection times and final size constrain R0 when the population at risk is known. Discrete DSA provides a simple, extensible framework for simulation and inference of infectious disease dynamics.

title: Retrospective Analysis of the VAERS Database for Children One Year of Age
abstract: In recent studies, novel candidate safety signals were detected for infants younger than 1 year of age for specific vaccines. Herein, the Vaccine Adverse Events Reporting System (VAERS) database was retrospectively examined for possible novel candidate safety signals for children one year of age. Novel candidate safety signals were detected for multiple vaccines. Two candidate manufacturing irregularities or possible unknown contaminants were identified associated with adverse event (AE) autism for VAERS nondomestic Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR II) vaccine lots from 1993 to 1995 and AE hyperpyrexia for nondomestic MMRV lots from 2019 to 2024. The candidate manufacturing irregularities were named alpha for MMR II and beta for Measles, Mumps, Rubella, and Varicella (MMRV) ProQuad vaccines. The hypothesized higher levels of alpha in the nondomestic data, MMR II appear to have been reduced or eliminated sometime soon after 1995; identification of alpha would contribute to future avoidance of possible associated AEs. Reduction of beta in the nondomestic MMRV vaccine is hypothesized to reduce hyperpyrexia and also higher pyrexia AEs not observed associated with domestic MMRV vaccine.

title: Strengthening catch-up vaccination delivery in routine health services for children under five in Western Kenya, 2022-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Catch-up vaccination can close population immunity gaps, yet integration into routine immunization services remains limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Following Kenya's 2023 catch-up vaccination policy, we evaluated a multi-strategy intervention to strengthen systematic identification, eligibility screening, and delivery of missed doses within routine health services in Siaya County. METHODS: Over 12 months, five strategies addressing healthcare worker (HCW) capacity, vaccination documentation, defaulter tracking, immunization screening, and caregiver engagement were implemented in 55 public health facilities selected through stratified random sampling. Using a pre-post design, we assessed immunization uptake, missed opportunities for vaccination (MOVs), and system readiness. Baseline (November 2022-January 2023) and endline (October-December 2024) evaluations included facility assessments, HCW interviews, caregiver exit surveys among children aged <36 months with home-based records (HBRs; n = 658), and facility immunization register abstractions (n = 1650 children aged 12-23 months). Analyses accounted for sampling design, clustering, and used generalized estimating equations for HBR data. RESULTS: MOV prevalence among children visiting facilities for any reason declined from 94.4% to 20.9% (p < 0.001). Full immunization among children aged 12-23 months increased from 44.9% to 63.6% (p < 0.001), with uptake improving across antigens. Measles-rubella first-dose uptake increased from 51.5% to 78.0%, and second-dose uptake from 18.8% to 36.9% (p < 0.001 for both). Eligibility screening expanded from 60.6% to 86.8% of facilities (p = 0.012), defaulter tracking improved from 48.5% to 91.6% (p < 0.001), and HCW knowledge and confidence increased significantly. CONCLUSION: The multi-strategy intervention was associated with fewer MOVs and improved uptake, suggesting that embedding catch-up vaccination within routine health services can strengthen immunization systems in decentralized LMIC contexts. Kenya's catch-up vaccination policy provided a framework for introducing catch-up vaccination into routine health services.

abstract_zh: 背景:追赶 疫苗接种 可以缩小人群免疫差距,但在低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC),融入常规免疫服务仍然有限。根据肯尼亚的 2023 年 疫苗接种 追赶政策,我们评估了一项多策略干预措施,以加强西亚县常规卫生服务中的系统识别、资格筛查和漏服剂量的提供。方法:在 12 个月的时间里,在通过分层随机抽样选出的 55 个公共卫生机构中实施了五项策略,涉及医疗保健工作者 (HCW) 能力、疫苗接种 文档、违约者跟踪、免疫筛查和护理人员参与。使用前后设计,我们评估了免疫接种率、疫苗接种 (MOV) 错过的机会以及系统准备情况。基线(2022 年 11 月至 2023 年 1 月)和终点(2024 年 10 月至 12 月)评估包括设施评估、医护人员访谈、对年龄 < 36 个月的儿童进行的护理人员退出调查(HBR;n = 658)以及设施免疫登记摘要(n = 1650 名 12-23 个月的儿童)。分析考虑了抽样设计、聚类,并使用了 HBR 数据的广义估计方程。结果:出于任何原因访问设施的儿童中 MOV 患病率 从 94.4% 下降至 20.9% (p < 0.001)。12-23 个月龄儿童的完全免疫率从 44.9% 增加到 63.6% (p < 0.001),各种抗原的吸收率有所提高。麻疹-风疹第一剂吸收率从 51.5% 增加到 78.0%,第二剂吸收率从 18.8% 增加到 36.9%(两者的 p < 0.001)。设施的资格筛查从 60.6% 扩大到 86.8% (p = 0.012),违约者跟踪从 48.5% 提高到 91.6% (p < 0.001),医护人员的知识和信心显着增加。结论:多策略干预与较少的 MOV 和提高的吸收率相关,这表明将追赶型 疫苗接种 纳入常规卫生服务可以加强分散的中低收入国家的免疫系统。肯尼亚的追赶型 疫苗接种 政策为将追赶型 疫苗接种 引入常规卫生服务提供了框架。

title: Advancements in oncolytic virus therapy: a new horizon for ovarian cancer
abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, and the limited durability of standard treatments has motivated the development of new therapeutic strategies. Oncolytic viruses selectively replicate within and lyse tumor cells, releasing tumor antigens and inflammatory signals that can convert an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment into an immune-inflamed state. This review evaluates the principal platforms used in ovarian cancer, including adenovirus, reovirus, measles virus, vaccinia virus, herpes simplex virus, and vesicular stomatitis virus. We compare engineering approaches that enhance tumor-selective replication, cellular entry, transgene delivery, and local immune activation, and discuss strategies to overcome neutralizing antibodies, restricted intratumoral spread, off-target toxicity, and tumor heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on cytokine- or bispecific T-cell engager-armed viruses and their combination with chemotherapy, immune checkpoint blockade, and cellular immunotherapy. Early-phase studies support the feasibility of intraperitoneal delivery, whereas a single-arm phase 2 study of Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy reported encouraging results, and a randomized phase 3 trial is ongoing. No oncolytic viruses have been approved for ovarian cancer; however, current evidence supports biomarker-guided and rationally sequenced clinical development.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 卵巢癌仍然是最致命的妇科恶性肿瘤,标准 治疗 有限的耐久性促进了新治疗策略的开发。本综述评估了用于卵巢癌的主要平台,包括 麻疹病毒,并讨论了它们与其他疗法结合的潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对卵巢癌溶瘤病毒平台(包括 麻疹病毒)的系统分析。它评估增强肿瘤选择性复制、细胞进入、转基因传递和局部免疫激活的工程方法。该综述还讨论了克服中和抗体、有限的瘤内扩散、脱靶毒性和肿瘤异质性的策略。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 早期研究支持腹腔内递送溶瘤病毒的可行性,Olvi-Vec 随后进行铂类化疗的单臂 2 期研究报告了令人鼓舞的结果。一项随机 3 期试验正在进行中,表明进一步评估基于 麻疹病毒 的卵巢癌疗法的潜力。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了中和抗体、有限的瘤内扩散、脱靶毒性和肿瘤异质性等挑战,这些挑战是溶瘤病毒有效性的障碍。这些问题仍未得到解决,需要进一步调查。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 特别强调细胞因子或双特异性 T 细胞接合病毒及其与化疗、免疫检查点阻断和细胞免疫疗法的组合。该综述表明,生物标志物引导和合理排序的临床开发对于推进基于 麻疹病毒 的卵巢癌治疗是必要的。

title: Travelers and Human–Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases
abstract: Background: International travel can accelerate the geographic spread of zoonotic pathogens and, under certain circumstances, contribute to epidemic or pandemic dissemination. Travelers may also transmit human pathogens to wildlife at tourism interfaces, acting as intermediaries in zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. Methods: Archived WHO and ECDC reports were screened for major zoonotic outbreaks in which international travel contributed to cross-border spread. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies of human-to-wildlife transmission involving tourists, visitors, or travelers and traveler behaviors that could facilitate transmission. Results: Among 14 major zoonotic outbreaks, travelers commonly acted as spreaders following initial animal-to-human spillover by importing infections into new regions, sometimes resulting in onward transmission. This pattern was prominent with respiratory infections such as SARS, MERS, influenza, and COVID-19 and vector-borne infections such as Oropouche and Zika. Twenty-one studies reported possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human–wildlife tourism interfaces. Pathogens included respiratory viruses, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, enteric pathogens, and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Affected wildlife included great apes, primates, elephants, felines, carnivorans, ungulates, avians, reptiles, and urban-adapted wildlife in national parks, zoological parks, rehabilitation centers, and semi-urban parks. Five additional studies documented risky tourist behaviors, including close approach to, physical contact with, and feeding and visiting wildlife while having respiratory symptoms, and inadequate vaccination against measles, influenza, and polio. Conclusions: Travelers can influence transmission bidirectionally by disseminating zoonotic pathogens and exposing wildlife to human pathogens. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization alongside conventional traveler protection.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of travelers in the transmission of zoonotic and reverse zoonotic diseases, with a focus on the measles virus. It explores how international travel can facilitate the spread of pathogens between humans and animals, and how human behaviors at wildlife interfaces may contribute to the transmission of human pathogens to wildlife.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilized archived WHO and ECDC reports to identify major zoonotic outbreaks involving international travel. It also conducted searches on PubMed and Scopus for studies on human-to-wildlife transmission and traveler behaviors that could facilitate such transmission.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Travelers can act as intermediaries in both zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission. They commonly import infections into new regions following initial animal-to-human spillover, which can lead to onward transmission. This pattern is particularly evident with respiratory infections such as measles, influenza, and others.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is evidence of travelers spreading zoonotic pathogens, the mechanisms and extent of reverse zoonotic transmission remain underexplored. Additionally, the role of specific behaviors, such as feeding wildlife or inadequate vaccination, in facilitating transmission is not fully quantified.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a need for targeted research on the role of traveler behaviors in reverse zoonotic transmission. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization to mitigate risks.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the bidirectional transmission of zoonotic and reverse zoonotic diseases involving travelers, with a focus on the measles virus. It highlights how international travel can accelerate the spread of pathogens between humans and animals, particularly respiratory viruses. The review identifies 14 major zoonotic outbreaks where travelers played a role in spreading infections, and 21 studies report possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human-wildlife interfaces. The review emphasizes the need for travel medicine to include wildlife-protective measures, such as hygiene and immunization, to reduce transmission risks. However, the mechanisms and extent of reverse zoonotic transmission remain underexplored, and further research is needed to address these gaps.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查利用世卫组织和欧洲疾病预防控制中心存档的报告来确定涉及国际旅行的主要人畜共患病 暴发。它还在 PubMed 和 Scopus 上搜索有关人类与野生动物 传播 以及可能促进此类 传播 的旅行者行为的研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 旅行者可以充当人畜共患病和反向人畜共患病 传播 的中介人。它们通常在最初的动物到人类 跨物种溢出 后将感染引入新区域,这可能导致后续的 传播。这种模式在 麻疹、流感等呼吸道感染中尤其明显。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然有证据表明旅行者传播人畜共患病原体,但反向人畜共患 传播 的机制和程度仍未得到充分研究。此外,特定行为(例如喂养野生动物或 疫苗接种 不足)在促进 传播 中的作用尚未完全量化。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要对旅行者行为在反向人畜共患病 传播 中的作用进行有针对性的研究。旅行医学应纳入有关距离、卫生、废物处理和免疫方面的野生动物保护咨询,以降低风险。

abstract_zh: 背景:国际旅行可以加速人畜共患病病原体的地理传播,并在某些情况下导致流行病或大流行的传播。旅行者还可能在旅游界面将人类病原体传播给野生动物,充当人畜共患和反向人畜共患 传播 的中介。方法:对存档的 WHO 和 ECDC 报告进行了筛查,以了解主要人畜共患病 暴发,其中国际旅行导致了跨境传播。在 PubMed 和 Scopus 中检索了有关人类与野生动物 传播 的研究,其中涉及游客、访客或可能促进 传播 的旅行者和旅行者行为。结果:在 14 种主要人畜共患 暴发 中,旅行者通常在最初的动物到人类 跨物种溢出 后充当传播者,将感染引入新地区,有时会导致进一步的 传播。这种模式在 SARS、MERS、流感和 COVID-19 等呼吸道感染以及 Oropouche 和 Zika 等 媒介 传播的感染中尤为突出。二十一项研究报告了人类与野生动物旅游界面可能或证实的反向人畜共患 传播。病原体包括呼吸道病毒、结核分枝杆菌、肠道病原体和耐药病原体。受影响的野生动物包括类人猿、灵长类动物、大象、猫科动物、食肉动物、有蹄类动物、鸟类、爬行动物以及国家公园、动物园、康复中心和半城市公园中适应城市的野生动物。另外五项研究记录了危险的游客行为,包括在出现呼吸道症状时近距离接近、身体接触、喂养和参观野生动物,以及针对 麻疹、流感和脊髓灰质炎的 麻疹 不足。结论:旅行者可以通过传播人畜共患病原体并使野生动物接触人类病原体来双向影响 传播。旅行医学应将有关距离、卫生、废物处理和免疫接种的野生动物保护咨询与传统的旅行者保护结合起来。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了旅行者在人畜共患疾病和反向人畜共患疾病 传播 中的作用,重点是 麻疹病毒。它探讨了国际旅行如何促进病原体在人类和动物之间的传播,以及人类在野生动物接触面的行为如何可能导致人类病原体传播给野生动物。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查利用世卫组织和欧洲疾病预防控制中心存档的报告来确定涉及国际旅行的主要人畜共患病 暴发。它还在 PubMed 和 Scopus 上搜索有关人类与野生动物 传播 以及可能促进此类 传播 的旅行者行为的研究。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 旅行者可以充当人畜共患病和反向人畜共患病 传播 的中介人。它们通常在最初的动物到人类 跨物种溢出 后将感染引入新区域,这可能导致后续的 传播。这种模式在 麻疹、流感等呼吸道感染中尤其明显。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然有证据表明旅行者传播人畜共患病原体,但反向人畜共患 传播 的机制和程度仍未得到充分研究。此外,特定行为(例如喂养野生动物或 疫苗接种 不足)在促进 传播 中的作用尚未完全量化。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要对旅行者行为在反向人畜共患病 传播 中的作用进行有针对性的研究。旅行医学应纳入有关距离、卫生、废物处理和免疫方面的野生动物保护咨询,以降低风险。

title: Comparison of routine health-facility (KHIS) versus house-survey (KDHS) estimates of childhood vaccination coverage in Kenya: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reliable estimates of effective coverage of health interventions are essential for tracking progress towards health goals and informing policy decisions. In settings where routine health information systems are limited, population-based household surveys are frequently used as reference standards. OBJECTIVE: This study compared national and sub-national childhood vaccination coverage estimates from Kenya's facility-based Health Information System (KHIS) and the 2022 Kenya Demographic Health Survey (KDHS) to assess concordance between the two data sources and to evaluate the suitability of routine data for programmatic decision-making. METHODS: We analysed BCG, pentavalent 1, pentavalent 3 and measles-rubella 1 (MR 1) vaccination data reported by 8178 health facilities to KHIS between March 2020 and March 2022 alongside KDHS 2022 data from 3679 children aged 12-23 months. Coverage estimates were compared at national and county levels using a two-proportion z-test. Absolute differences in coverage were categorised as minimal ( 10%) occurred in 9-14 counties. Only three counties showed absolute differences <5% across all four antigens; several counties showed persistent divergence across antigens. CONCLUSION: KHIS yields reasonably concordant national-level estimates of childhood vaccination coverage, but substantial and uneven county-level discrepancies limit its reliability for sub-national decision-making. A differentiated approach is warranted: KHIS can support national trend monitoring and may be usable in counties with demonstrated concordance, whereas counties with persistent divergence require continued survey-based validation and targeted strengthening of routine data systems. The two data sources should not be treated as interchangeable at county level.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在比较肯尼亚基于设施的健康信息系统 (KHIS) 和 2022 年肯尼亚人口健康调查 (KDHS) 的国家和次国家儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值,以评估两个数据源之间的一致性,并评估常规数据对规划决策的适用性。对健康干预措施有效覆盖范围的可靠估计对于跟踪健康目标的进展情况和为政策决策提供信息至关重要,特别是在常规卫生信息系统有限且经常使用基于人口的家庭调查作为参考标准的环境中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了来自 3679 名 12-23 个月儿童的 KHIS 和 KDHS 2022 数据的国家和次国家儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值。该分析包括 2020 年 3 月至 2022 年 3 月期间 8178 个卫生机构向 KHIS 报告的 BCG、五价 1、五价 3 和 麻疹-风疹 1 (MR 1) 疫苗接种 数据。
elements_zh.methods: 使用二比例 z 检验在国家和县一级比较覆盖率估计值。覆盖率的绝对差异分为最小(≤5%)或显着(>5%)。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有三个县的所有四种抗原的绝对差异<5%;几个县的抗原表现出持续的差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: KHIS 得出了相当一致的国家级儿童 疫苗接种 覆盖率估计值,但县级的巨大且不均匀的差异限制了其在地方决策中的可靠性。需要采取差异化的方法:KHIS 可以支持国家趋势监测,并且可用于具有一致性的县,而持续存在差异的县则需要继续基于调查的验证并有针对性地加强常规数据系统。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,虽然 KHIS 可以提供可靠的国家级估计,但未经进一步验证,它不适合地方决策。这对 疫苗 可预防疾病的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 具有影响,特别是与 ZX​​QTERMEQXZ 密切相关的 麻疹。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括潜在的偏差和混杂因素,以及样本量和普遍性。由于研究设计的局限性以及需要在存在持续分歧的县进行进一步验证,证据强度中等。

title: Could Microarray Patch Vaccines Contribute to Pandemic Preparedness? Opportunities, Implementation Considerations, and Priorities
abstract: Microarray patches (MAPs) demonstrate potential to improve pandemic preparedness by supporting rapid and large-scale vaccine distribution and administration, particularly in settings with limited cold-chain capacity or health workforce resources. This narrative review synthesises preclinical and clinical MAP vaccine research alongside literature on product development, manufacturing, regulation, implementation, acceptability, and equitable access, and reports encouraging early-phase tolerability and immunogenicity findings for influenza, Japanese encephalitis, measles–rubella, and SARS-CoV-2 MAP vaccines. Notable advantages include improved thermostability, antigen dose sparing, simplified application, the possibility of self- or layperson administration, reduced reliance on trained vaccinators, and suitability for outreach and low-resource settings. Advancing MAP technology requires selection of target vaccines, development of stable, antigen-specific formulations, confirmation of dose delivery, completion of phased clinical trials and regulatory assessments, establishment of scalable, quality-controlled manufacturing systems, and integration into immunization programmes. Challenges involve antigen compatibility, dose consistency, formulation stability, manufacturing scale-up, regulatory requirements, uncertain costs and commercial incentives, public acceptance, and equitable access. Following licensure, Phase IV surveillance and effectiveness studies will be needed to evaluate real-world safety and performance. Investment across research, manufacturing, regulation, and delivery is essential to position MAPs as complementary tools to conventional vaccines, thus broadening the speed, reach, and flexibility of pandemic immunization responses.

abstract_zh: 微阵列贴片 (MAP) 通过支持快速和大规模的 疫苗 分发和管理,显示出改善大流行病防备的潜力,特别是在冷链能力或卫生劳动力资源有限的环境中。这篇叙述性综述综合了临床前和临床 MAP 疫苗 研究以及有关产品开发、制造、监管、实施、可接受性和公平获取的文献,并报告了流感、日本脑炎、麻疹-风疹和 SARS-CoV-2 MAP 疫苗 的令人鼓舞的早期耐受性和免疫原性发现。显着的优点包括提高热稳定性、节省抗原剂量、简化应用、自我或非专业人士给药的可能性、减少对训练有素的疫苗接种人员的依赖以及适合外展和资源匮乏的环境。推进 MAP 技术需要选择靶点 疫苗、开发稳定的抗原特异性制剂、确认剂量输送、完成分阶段临床试验和监管评估、建立可扩展的、质量控制的制造系统,并整合到免疫计划中。挑战包括抗原相容性、剂量一致性、配方稳定性、生产规模扩大、监管要求、不确定的成本和商业激励、公众接受度和公平获取。获得许可后,将需要进行第四阶段 监测 和有效性研究来评估现实世界的安全性和性能。研究、制造、监管和交付方面的投资对于将 MAP 定位为传统 疫苗 的补充工具至关重要,从而扩大大流行免疫反应的速度、范围和灵活性。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇叙述性综述综合了 MAP 疫苗 的临床前和临床研究,包括流感、日本脑炎、麻疹-风疹和 SARS-CoV-2 的研究。它还包含有关产品开发、制造、监管、实施、可接受性和公平获取的文献。该审查不报告具体数据库、检索日期或资格标准。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,MAP 疫苗 对 麻疹 和其他相关病原体显示出令人鼓舞的早期耐受性和免疫原性发现。显着的优点包括提高热稳定性、节省抗原剂量、简化应用以及适合资源匮乏的环境。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了推进 MAP 技术的挑战,包括抗原兼容性、剂量一致性、配方稳定性、生产规模扩大、监管要求以及不确定的成本和商业激励。这些问题代表了需要进一步调查的证据差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 获得许可后,审查建议需要进行 IV 期 监测 和有效性研究,以评估现实世界的安全性和性能。跨研究、制造、监管和交付的投资对于将 MAP 定位为传统 疫苗 的补充工具至关重要。

title: Human Capital Development and Economic Growth in Nigeria: An Application of Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) Model Approach
abstract: This study examined the impact of human capital development on economic growth in Nigeria from 1990 to 2020. The study adopted an ex post facto research design, to make an empirical investigation on the impact of human capital development proxy by Immunization against measles, infant mortality rate, and government expenditure on health and education as well as total energy consumption and on economic growth proxy by the growth rate of GDP. The study employed the ADF unit root test; the bounds test approach to cointegration, ARDL long and Short-run estimations as well as some post-estimation tests. Accordingly, the unit root test result showed that the variables under consideration are integrated at different orders 1 and 0. The bound test confirmed the presence of a long-run relationship among the variables under discourse. The ARDL estimation in the long run showed that a 1% decrease in infant mortality resulted in a 0.91% increase in GDPG. Also, a 1% increase in government expenditure on education and health increased GDPG by 0.23% and 0.05% respectively. The study recommended the prioritization of investment in education and healthcare to reduce infant mortality rates.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: A multi-region discrete time chain binomial model for infectious disease transmission
abstract: Conventional mathematical models of infectious diseases often overlook the spatial spread of the disease, focusing only on local transmission. However, spatial propagation of various diseases has been observed mainly due to the movement of infectious individuals from one region to another. In this work, we propose a multiregion discrete-time chain binomial framework to model dependencies between infection time series from neighboring regions. The proposed model is based on the epidemiological principle that new infections arise from interactions between susceptible and previously infected individuals. To strengthen the statistical formulation, the probability of new infections within each spatial unit is modeled through a link function, by allowing it to depend on lagged local incidence, inter-regional transmission effects, and region-specific covariates. The framework also allows for higher-order temporal dependence through an AR(p) specification. To reduce complexity of the model as the number of regions increases, sparsity is imposed by using spatial contiguity matrices and k-nearest-neighbor structures. For estimating these multiregion models, an appropriate likelihood function maximization approach is proposed. A predictive likelihood based method is used to generate forecasts of disease counts in connected spatial units. In-depth analyses of two real measles datasets and simulation studies incorporating seasonal patterns, different weight matrices across connected regions, and varying intervention strategies are used to motivate the proposed modeling framework and demonstrate its ability to reproduce realistic outbreak dynamics. While the simulation studies demonstrate applicability of the general AR(p) approach, the real data analysis of measles shows that an AR(1) model is adequate to capture the temporal dependence.

abstract_original: Conventional mathematical models of infectious diseases often overlook the spatial spread of the disease, focusing only on local transmission. However, spatial propagation of various diseases has been observed mainly due to the movement of infectious individuals from one region to another. In this work, we propose a multiregion discrete-time chain binomial framework to model dependencies between infection time series from neighboring regions. The proposed model is based on the epidemiological principle that new infections arise from interactions between susceptible and previously infected individuals. To strengthen the statistical formulation, the probability of new infections within each spatial unit is modeled through a link function, by allowing it to depend on lagged local incidence, inter-regional transmission effects, and region-specific covariates. The framework also allows for higher-order temporal dependence through an AR(p) specification. To reduce complexity of the model as the number of regions increases, sparsity is imposed by using spatial contiguity matrices and k-nearest-neighbor structures. For estimating these multiregion models, an appropriate likelihood function maximization approach is proposed. A predictive likelihood based method is used to generate forecasts of disease counts in connected spatial units. In-depth analyses of two real measles datasets and simulation studies incorporating seasonal patterns, different weight matrices across connected regions, and varying intervention strategies are used to motivate the proposed modeling framework and demonstrate its ability to reproduce realistic outbreak dynamics. While the simulation studies demonstrate applicability of the general AR(p) approach, the real data analysis of measles shows that an AR(1) model is adequate to capture the temporal dependence.
title_original: A multi-region discrete time chain binomial model for infectious disease transmission

source_body_en: Conventional mathematical models of infectious diseases often overlook the spatial spread of the disease, focusing only on local transmission. However, spatial propagation of various diseases has been observed mainly due to the movement of infectious individuals from one region to another. The framework also allows for higher-order temporal dependence through an AR(p) specification. In-depth analyses of two real measles datasets and simulation studies incorporating seasonal patterns, different weight matrices across connected regions, and varying intervention strategies are used to motivate the proposed modeling framework and demonstrate its ability to reproduce realistic outbreak dynamics. full_text: Article summary The resurgence of measles in Bangladesh in 2026 highlights the fragility of immunization systems, revealing how quickly gains in disease elimination can be reversed due to declining vaccination coverage and systemic failures. This paper outlines the outbreak's drivers and consequences, emphasizing the urgent need for policy reforms focused on equitable vaccine access, improved governance, and robust immunization strategies to prevent future crises. Abstract Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in decades, with more than 50,500 suspected cases and at least 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths during the reporting period from mid-March to mid-May 2026. After years of progress that had sharply reduced measles incidence, this resurgence reflects not a biological inevitability but a preventable systems failure. A nationwide Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine stockout in 2024 to 2025, the absence of nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) since 2020, declining MR1 and MR2 coverage, and widening subnational inequities have combined to erode population immunity. The burden has fallen disproportionately on zero-dose and under-vaccinated children in urban slums, hard-to-reach rural areas, and refugee camps, especially infants too young for routine vaccination. Positioned within the broader post-COVID global resurgence, Bangladesh’s epidemic highlights measles as a sentinel of weakening immunization resilience. The crisis underscores three transferable lessons for countries facing declining coverage: maintain buffer stocks and diversified procurement to prevent stockouts, prioritize catch-up SIAs when routine coverage falters, and embed equity-focused outreach to reach zero-dose children before outbreaks occur. This perspective article delves into the structural reforms needed in vaccine governance and procurement, the restoration of routine and catch-up immunization services with equity at their center, and the transparent accountability required to address the failures that created the current immunity gap. Similar content being viewed by others 1 Introduction Globally, measles remains a major threat despite an available vaccine, with an estimated 11 million cases and 95,000 deaths in 2024 and outbreaks reported in 59 countries, underscoring WHO’s recommendation that ≥ 95% coverage with two measles-containing vaccine doses is required to interrupt transmission [1]. Bangladesh was long seen as a regional model for measles control, with substantial gains driven by sustained routine immunization and periodic supplementary campaigns. Yet the country is now confronting one of its most severe measles outbreaks in decades, exposing how quickly immunization gains can unravel when coverage declines, vaccine supply is disrupted, and inequities persist [2, 3]. This resurgence has had devastating consequences for children, particularly in underserved and hard-to-reach communities where routine services are weakest and vulnerability is highest [4]. This perspective examines the drivers of Bangladesh’s 2026 measles resurgence, situates it within the wider post-COVID global rebound in measles, and argues that durable control will require equity-centered reform of immunization governance, delivery, and accountability. It further contends that the outbreak should be read not as an isolated epidemiologic event, but as a warning signal of broader fragility in child health systems and public health preparedness [5]. 2 Reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains 2.1 Earlier progress towards elimination In the early 2000s, measles remained a leading cause of child mortality in Bangladesh, with national first dose of measles‐containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage stagnating at or below 75% and no district achieving the 95% threshold required for population-level protection. Through sustained investment in EPI, linkage with child health days and vitamin A campaigns, and repeated nationwide SIAs, Bangladesh raised MCV1 coverage from roughly 74–89% in 2000 to more than 94–118% (administrative) by 2016. At the same time, a routine second dose (MCV2) was introduced in 2012 and the coverage of MCV2 increased from roughly one-third of children to over 90% by the mid-2010s. Over the same period, confirmed measles incidence declined by more than 80%, decreasing from approximately 40 cases per million population to 6 per million, and large outbreaks became rare [6, 7]. At the regional level, the WHO South-East Asia Region established targets for measles elimination and rubella control. Bangladesh aligned with these goals, committing to elimination timelines initially set for 2018 and subsequently extended, thereby firmly integrating measles control into national child survival strategies and Universal Health Coverage priorities. These achievements positioned Bangladesh as a model of immunization success in a low-income setting and fostered momentum toward increasingly ambitious elimination targets [6, 8]. 2.2 Slow erosion of population immunity Behind this success story, however, vulnerabilities began to accumulate. WHO and national surveillance data indicate that although national MR1 and MR2 coverage remained relatively high, both measures plateaued and then fell modestly after 2019, MR1 from about 88–89% to 86%, and MR2 from roughly 89% to 80.7% by 2023–2024, leaving an estimated 20 million children partially or fully unprotected during this period [9]. These national averages masked substantial subnational inequities. Urban slums, hard-to-reach rural unions, and humanitarian settings, including the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, continued to harbor concentrations of zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, underscoring persistent access and equity gaps despite overall coverage gains. Moreover, although Bangladesh historically conducted SIAs at roughly four-year intervals, no nationwide MR campaign was carried out after 2020, largely because of pandemic-related disruptions and subsequent political instability [10, 11]. 3 The 2024 to 2025 MR vaccine stockout, a preventable disruption 3.1 Procurement disruption and stockout Multiple reports from WHO, UNICEF, and subsequent investigations suggest that disruptions in MR vaccine supply and immunization delivery during 2024–2025 may have contributed to the accumulation of susceptible children before the 2026 outbreak. Following the 2024 political transition, changes in procurement arrangements and reported administrative delays were associated with vaccine stockouts and interruptions in routine immunization [2, 12]. A supplementary MR campaign postponed in 2024 was reportedly not implemented in 2025 and was subsequently cancelled. Available coverage estimates are inconsistent: WHO–UNICEF reported MR1 and MR2 coverage of 97% and 93% in 2023, whereas some national reports cited a decline to approximately 56–59% in 2025 [13, 14]. These discrepancies may reflect differences in data sources and methods. Overall, the evidence suggests, but does not establish that these disruptions likely expanded the susceptible population and facilitated the outbreak’s scale. 3.2 Missed SIAs and compounded immunity gaps The stockout occurred against the backdrop of missed SIAs after 2020, when COVID-19 and subsequent political unrest delayed the usual four-yearly nationwide campaigns. Without these catch-up campaigns to reach zero-dose and missed children, each year of modest under‐coverage added to a growing cohort of susceptible children. By early 2026, WHO estimated that suboptimal MR1 and MR2 coverage, combined with the absence of SIAs and the 2024–2025 vaccine stockout, had significantly increased the number of susceptible children. This convergence of vulnerabilities created favorable conditions for sustained measles transmission once the virus reentered the population. The measles virus, being one of the most contagious pathogens known, readily exploits such immunity gaps, and outbreaks are often the earliest visible indication of deeper fragility in the immunization system [15, 16]. 4 Epidemiologic scale and clinical burden of the 2026 measles outbreak 4.1 Epidemiology and severity On 4 April 2026, Bangladesh’s National International Health Regulations (IHR) Focal Point notified WHO of a nationwide increase in measles cases. By 11 May 2026, DGHS data reported 50,500 suspected cases and 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths, giving a crude reported death-to-suspected-case ratio of approximately 0.82% [2]. The majority of cases, approximately 79%, occurred in children under five years of age, including 66% in those under two years and about one-third in infants younger than nine months, an age group that is not yet eligible for routine measles vaccination. Subsequent situation reports from national authorities, the World Health Organization, and humanitarian partners indicate sustained expansion of the outbreak. Between 22 April and 4 May 2026, reported cumulative suspected measles cases in Bangladesh rose from 27,164 to 41,793, while laboratory-confirmed cases increased from 3,934 to 5,467. Over the same period, the reported combined toll of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths rose from 190 to 311. Children under five accounted for approximately 80% of reported cases as of 19 April [17]. Daily hospital admissions have, at times, exceeded 1,200–1,300 cases, overwhelming pediatric services and exposing critical shortages in isolation capacity, healthcare personnel, and diagnostic resources [2, 18]. Measles-associated complications, including pneumonia, diarrhoea, and severe disease linked to malnutrition, are frequently reported, particularly among undernourished children and those lacking vitamin A supplementation. This pattern is consistent with global evidence demonstrating that measles-related mortality disproportionately affects vulnerable, malnourished populations. Although precise case fatality ratios vary by setting and surveillance sensitivity, the concentration of deaths among unvaccinated and under-vaccinated children under two years of age underscores the largely preventable nature of this burden [19]. 4.2 Spatial concentration and social determinants The outbreak has attained extensive geographic spread, affecting 58 of 64 districts, approximately 91%, across all eight divisions, while remaining highly concentrated in specific hotspots (Fig. 1). Dhaka division alone has reported over 18,000 to 19,000 cases in several situation reports, with substantial burdens also observed in Rajshahi, Chattogram, and Khulna. Within Dhaka, cases are concentrated in densely populated informal settlements and industrial slums, including Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon, where crowding, poverty, and highly mobile populations complicate the delivery of routine health services [2, 20]. Humanitarian settings, particularly the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, constitute a major concern during the 2026 measles outbreak in Bangladesh. In the camps, measles transmission was documented early in the outbreak and then escalated rapidly, with reports noting 19 suspected cases in January, 199 in February, 76 suspected cases with 8 laboratory-confirmed cases by March, and 239 suspected cases tested with 60 confirmed cases and 5 associated deaths by 14 May 2026. By 20 May 2026, the camp setting had reported 595 suspected and 60 confirmed cases, underscoring the intense transmission potential in a population with constrained access to routine services, heavy reliance on humanitarian assistance, high baseline malnutrition, large zero-dose cohorts, and frequent population movement. These conditions create a setting highly conducive to explosive measles spread and severe clinical outcomes [2, 21]. 5 Determinants of the catastrophe 5.1 Programmatic and health‐system determinants From a programmatic perspective, three interlocking determinants stand out. Suboptimal routine immunization coverage and missed SIAs have created a major vulnerability, as measles elimination requires at least 95% two-dose coverage in every district. Available estimates suggest that MR1 and MR2 coverage in Bangladesh may have declined to approximately 57–59% in 2025, potentially leaving a substantial susceptible population and facilitating sustained transmission. Reported nationwide MR vaccine stockouts during 2024–2025, reportedly associated with changes in procurement arrangements and administrative delays, may represent an important health-system weakness that contributed to reduced immunization opportunities and may have affected public confidence in services. In addition, possible gaps in surveillance and delays in recognizing early increases in measles incidence during late 2025 and early 2026 may have limited the timeliness of national alerting and pre-emptive campaigns, although the precise contribution of these factors is difficult to establish from the available evidence. These programmatic challenges may reflect broader health-system constraints, including potentially inadequate buffer stocks and contingency planning, limited operational flexibility of the EPI, and persistent underinvestment in peripheral human resources and cold-chain capacity; further evaluation is needed to confirm their relative contributions to the outbreak [22]. 5.2 Social and structural determinants Social determinants strongly shaped both measles exposure and outcomes in Bangladesh during the 2026 outbreak. Children living in urban slums, peri-urban settlements, and remote rural areas faced multiple barriers to vaccination, including distance to facilities, opportunity costs for caregivers in informal work, gendered constraints on women’s mobility, and low trust in preventive services amid precarious livelihoods. These structural barriers were not evenly distributed: WHO reported that the outbreak’s cumulative burden in Dhaka was concentrated in dense informal settlements, including Demra, Jatrabari, Kamrangirchar, Korail, Mirpur, and Tejgaon, underscoring how overcrowding and deprivation amplified transmission risk. Similarly, a WHO-supported campaign in Gopalganj identified at least 16 eligible children from mobile “floating” families who had missed both routine immunization and the outbreak campaign entirely, illustrating how mobile and marginalized households can remain outside the reach of standard delivery systems. These same children are also more likely to be undernourished, vitamin A deficient, and living in overcrowded housing, increasing both infection risk and disease severity once infected. The crisis further exposed inequities in humanitarian protection: Rohingya children in the camps, undocumented migrants, and mobile populations along the India and Myanmar borders were repeatedly at risk of being missed by routine services and campaigns, while large zero-dose cohorts and cross-border mobility continued to sustain transmission [2, 23]. 6 Post-COVID global measles resurgence Bangladesh’s outbreak is part of a broader global resurgence rather than an isolated event. Regional comparisons underscore that Bangladesh’s 2026 outbreak was part of a wider measles resurgence in South-East Asia, with WHO documenting outbreaks or increases in measles cases in India, Nepal, Thailand, and Maldives, and Myanmar strengthening measles preparedness in border areas because of spillover risk from Bangladesh. In the post-COVID period, measles has re-expanded sharply worldwide, and WHO reported that 59 countries experienced large or disruptive outbreaks in 2024, nearly three times the number in 2021, including several that had previously achieved elimination. Global MCV1 coverage in 2024, at approximately 84 to 86%, and MCV2 coverage, at about 76%, remained below pre pandemic levels and far short of the 95% two dose threshold needed to interrupt transmission. The Bangladesh epidemic thus exemplifies a broader pattern: measles serves as a sensitive indicator of weaknesses in immunization systems, because its extreme contagiousness means that even small gaps in routine coverage or outbreak response can rapidly lead to sustained transmission. Even modest and sustained declines in coverage, especially when compounded by missed campaigns, can quickly accumulate large susceptible cohorts and precipitate explosive outbreaks once importation or reemergence occurs [2, 24, 25]. 7 Policy and governance implications 7.1 Accountability for procurement and stock management Reports of vaccine procurement delays and stockouts, alongside indications of reduced measles vaccination coverage in 2025, raise questions about the continuity and governance of Bangladesh’s immunization programme [25]. Reporting in May 2026 suggested that proposed changes to established procurement arrangements may have contributed to supply delays, although the nature and effects of those changes remained contested. Leaders of the newly elected government also discussed responsibility across previous administrations and interim authorities in parliamentary remarks. Taken together, these accounts point to a need to examine procurement decisions and their possible contribution to coverage gaps, rather than to presume a single cause. They also highlight the value of clearly assigned procurement authority, transparent stock monitoring, adequate buffer inventories, and continuity plans to protect EPI vaccine supply during policy or institutional transitions [26]. 7.2 Communication, trust, and community engagement Unlike in some high-income countries, available evidence suggests that widespread anti-vaccine sentiment is not the principal driver of measles resurgence in Bangladesh. Instead, most available reports emphasize structural access and supply barriers more than active refusal. full_text_sections.full_text: Article summary The resurgence of measles in Bangladesh in 2026 highlights the fragility of immunization systems, revealing how quickly gains in disease elimination can be reversed due to declining vaccination coverage and systemic failures. This paper outlines the outbreak's drivers and consequences, emphasizing the urgent need for policy reforms focused on equitable vaccine access, improved governance, and robust immunization strategies to prevent future crises. Abstract Bangladesh is experiencing its worst measles outbreak in decades, with more than 50,500 suspected cases and at least 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths during the reporting period from mid-March to mid-May 2026. After years of progress that had sharply reduced measles incidence, this resurgence reflects not a biological inevitability but a preventable systems failure. A nationwide Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine stockout in 2024 to 2025, the absence of nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) since 2020, declining MR1 and MR2 coverage, and widening subnational inequities have combined to erode population immunity. The burden has fallen disproportionately on zero-dose and under-vaccinated children in urban slums, hard-to-reach rural areas, and refugee camps, especially infants too young for routine vaccination. Positioned within the broader post-COVID global resurgence, Bangladesh’s epidemic highlights measles as a sentinel of weakening immunization resilience. The crisis underscores three transferable lessons for countries facing declining coverage: maintain buffer stocks and diversified procurement to prevent stockouts, prioritize catch-up SIAs when routine coverage falters, and embed equity-focused outreach to reach zero-dose children before outbreaks occur. This perspective article delves into the structural reforms needed in vaccine governance and procurement, the restoration of routine and catch-up immunization services with equity at their center, and the transparent accountability required to address the failures that created the current immunity gap. Similar content being viewed by others 1 Introduction Globally, measles remains a major threat despite an available vaccine, with an estimated 11 million cases and 95,000 deaths in 2024 and outbreaks reported in 59 countries, underscoring WHO’s recommendation that ≥ 95% coverage with two measles-containing vaccine doses is required to interrupt transmission [1]. Bangladesh was long seen as a regional model for measles control, with substantial gains driven by sustained routine immunization and periodic supplementary campaigns. Yet the country is now confronting one of its most severe measles outbreaks in decades, exposing how quickly immunization gains can unravel when coverage declines, vaccine supply is disrupted, and inequities persist [2, 3]. This resurgence has had devastating consequences for children, particularly in underserved and hard-to-reach communities where routine services are weakest and vulnerability is highest [4]. This perspective examines the drivers of Bangladesh’s 2026 measles resurgence, situates it within the wider post-COVID global rebound in measles, and argues that durable control will require equity-centered reform of immunization governance, delivery, and accountability. It further contends that the outbreak should be read not as an isolated epidemiologic event, but as a warning signal of broader fragility in child health systems and public health preparedness [5]. 2 Reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains 2.1 Earlier progress towards elimination In the early 2000s, measles remained a leading cause of child mortality in Bangladesh, with national first dose of measles‐containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage stagnating at or below 75% and no district achieving the 95% threshold required for population-level protection. Through sustained investment in EPI, linkage with child health days and vitamin A campaigns, and repeated nationwide SIAs, Bangladesh raised MCV1 coverage from roughly 74–89% in 2000 to more than 94–118% (administrative) by 2016. At the same time, a routine second dose (MCV2) was introduced in 2012 and the coverage of MCV2 increased from roughly one-third of children to over 90% by the mid-2010s. Over the same period, confirmed measles incidence declined by more than 80%, decreasing from approximately 40 cases per million population to 6 per million, and large outbreaks became rare [6, 7]. At the regional level, the WHO South-East Asia Region established targets for measles elimination and rubella control. Bangladesh aligned with these goals, committing to elimination timelines initially set for 2018 and subsequently extended, thereby firmly integrating measles control into national child survival strategies and Universal Health Coverage priorities. These achievements positioned Bangladesh as a model of immunization success in a low-income setting and fostered momentum toward increasingly ambitious elimination targets [6, 8]. 2.2 Slow erosion of population immunity Behind this success story, however, vulnerabilities began to accumulate. WHO and national surveillance data indicate that although national MR1 and MR2 coverage remained relatively high, both measures plateaued and then fell modestly after 2019, MR1 from about 88–89% to 86%, and MR2 from roughly 89% to 80.7% by 2023–2024, leaving an estimated 20 million children partially or fully unprotected during this period [9]. These national averages masked substantial subnational inequities. Urban slums, hard-to-reach rural unions, and humanitarian settings, including the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, continued to harbor concentrations of zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, underscoring persistent access and equity gaps despite overall coverage gains. Moreover, although Bangladesh historically conducted SIAs at roughly four-year intervals, no nationwide MR campaign was carried out after 2020, largely because of pandemic-related disruptions and subsequent political instability [10, 11]. 3 The 2024 to 2025 MR vaccine stockout, a preventable disruption 3.1 Procurement disruption and stockout Multiple reports from WHO, UNICEF, and subsequent investigations suggest that disruptions in MR vaccine supply and immunization delivery during 2024–2025 may have contributed to the accumulation of susceptible children before the 2026 outbreak. Following the 2024 political transition, changes in procurement arrangements and reported administrative delays were associated with vaccine stockouts and interruptions in routine immunization [2, 12]. A supplementary MR campaign postponed in 2024 was reportedly not implemented in 2025 and was subsequently cancelled. Available coverage estimates are inconsistent: WHO–UNICEF reported MR1 and MR2 coverage of 97% and 93% in 2023, whereas some national reports cited a decline to approximately 56–59% in 2025 [13, 14]. These discrepancies may reflect differences in data sources and methods. Overall, the evidence suggests, but does not establish that these disruptions likely expanded the susceptible population and facilitated the outbreak’s scale. 3.2 Missed SIAs and compounded immunity gaps The stockout occurred against the backdrop of missed SIAs after 2020, when COVID-19 and subsequent political unrest delayed the usual four-yearly nationwide campaigns. Without these catch-up campaigns to reach zero-dose and missed children, each year of modest under‐coverage added to a growing cohort of susceptible children. By early 2026, WHO estimated that suboptimal MR1 and MR2 coverage, combined with the absence of SIAs and the 2024–2025 vaccine stockout, had significantly increased the number of susceptible children. This convergence of vulnerabilities created favorable conditions for sustained measles transmission once the virus reentered the population. title_original: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh 2026 undermines elimination gains and requires urgent policy action

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh, which undermines previous elimination gains and necessitates urgent policy action. The background highlights the ongoing threat of measles globally, despite the availability of a vaccine, and the importance of achieving high vaccination coverage to interrupt transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examines the reversal of Bangladesh’s measles elimination gains, focusing on the period from the early 2000s to 2026. It includes a population of children in Bangladesh, with data collected through sustained investment in the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), linkage with child health days, and repeated nationwide supplementary immunization activities (SIAs).
analysis.methods: The methods involve the analysis of national and WHO surveillance data, including coverage estimates of measles-containing vaccines (MCV1 and MCV2), and the examination of reported cases and deaths. The study also considers the impact of changes in procurement arrangements and administrative delays on vaccine stockouts and routine immunization.
analysis.main_results: The main results show a significant increase in measles cases and deaths in early 2026, with 50,500 suspected cases and 415 confirmed or suspected measles-related deaths. The majority of cases occurred in children under five years of age, with a high concentration in Dhaka division. The study also reports a decline in routine immunization coverage and the absence of SIAs, which contributed to the resurgence of measles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating a major vulnerability in Bangladesh’s measles elimination efforts, with suboptimal coverage and missed SIAs creating a susceptible population. The study highlights the need for urgent policy action to address these issues and prevent further outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution that the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh has significant implications for public health, including the potential for further spread and the need for enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts. The study underscores the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage to prevent measles outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations, including inconsistent coverage estimates and the potential for delays in recognizing early increases in measles incidence. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on reported data and the absence of specific methodological details.

analysis.summary_en: The study examines the resurgence of measles in Bangladesh, which undermines previous elimination gains and necessitates urgent policy action. Key findings include a significant increase in cases and deaths, with suboptimal vaccination coverage and missed SIAs contributing to the resurgence. The study highlights the need for enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts to prevent further outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究涉及孟加拉国 麻疹 的死灰复燃,这破坏了之前的消除成果,需要采取紧急政策行动。尽管存在 疫苗,但背景强调了 麻疹 在全球范围内的持续威胁,以及实现高 疫苗接种 覆盖率以中断 传播 的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究考察了孟加拉国 麻疹 消除成果的逆转,重点关注 2000 年代初至 2026 年期间。它包括孟加拉国的儿童人口,通过对扩大免疫计划 (EPI) 的持续投资、与儿童健康日的联系以及重复的全国补充免疫活动 (SIA) 收集数据。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对国家和世卫组织 监测 数据的分析,包括包含 麻疹 的 疫苗(MCV1 和 MCV2)的覆盖率估计,以及对报告病例和死亡的检查。该研究还考虑了采购安排的变化和行政延误对 疫苗 缺货和常规免疫接种的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要结果显示,2026年初麻疹病例和死亡人数显着增加,疑似病例50,500例,确诊或疑似麻疹相关死亡415例。大多数病例发生在五岁以下儿童,其中最集中在达卡区。该研究还报告了常规免疫覆盖率的下降和 SIA 的缺乏,这导致了 麻疹 的死灰复燃。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为孟加拉国 麻疹 消除工作的一个重大漏洞,覆盖范围不理想且错过了 SIA,从而造成了易感人群。该研究强调需要采取紧急政策行动来解决这些问题并防止进一步的 暴发。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果警告说,麻疹 在孟加拉国的死灰复燃对公共卫生具有重大影响,包括进一步传播的可能性以及加强 监测 和 疫苗接种 工作的必要性。该研究强调了保持高 疫苗接种 覆盖率以预防 麻疹 暴发 的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认其局限性,包括覆盖范围估计不一致以及延迟识别 麻疹 发病率 早期增加的可能性。由于依赖报告的数据且缺乏具体的方法学细节,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究涉及孟加拉国 麻疹 的死灰复燃,这破坏了之前的消除成果,需要采取紧急政策行动。尽管存在 疫苗,但背景强调了 麻疹 在全球范围内的持续威胁,以及实现高 疫苗接种 覆盖率以中断 传播 的重要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究考察了孟加拉国 麻疹 消除成果的逆转,重点关注 2000 年代初至 2026 年期间。它包括孟加拉国的儿童人口,通过对扩大免疫计划 (EPI) 的持续投资、与儿童健康日的联系以及重复的全国补充免疫活动 (SIA) 收集数据。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对国家和世卫组织 监测 数据的分析,包括包含 麻疹 的 疫苗(MCV1 和 MCV2)的覆盖率估计,以及对报告病例和死亡的检查。该研究还考虑了采购安排的变化和行政延误对 疫苗 缺货和常规免疫接种的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 主要结果显示,2026年初麻疹病例和死亡人数显着增加,疑似病例50,500例,确诊或疑似麻疹相关死亡415例。大多数病例发生在五岁以下儿童,其中最集中在达卡区。该研究还报告了常规免疫覆盖率的下降和 SIA 的缺乏,这导致了 麻疹 的死灰复燃。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为孟加拉国 麻疹 消除工作的一个重大漏洞,覆盖范围不理想且错过了 SIA,从而造成了易感人群。该研究强调需要采取紧急政策行动来解决这些问题并防止进一步的 暴发。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认其局限性,包括覆盖范围估计不一致以及延迟识别 麻疹 发病率 早期增加的可能性。由于依赖报告的数据且缺乏具体的方法学细节,证据强度中等。

full_text: Dear Editor, Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent infection of the central nervous system by a mutated measles virus.[] The disease classically presents with cognitive decline, behavioral deterioration, progressive impairment of scholastic performance, and stereotyped periodic myoclonus.[,] However, accumulating evidence indicates that the clinical spectrum of SSPE is considerably broader than previously recognized, and movement disorders may occasionally dominate the clinical presentation, leading to substantial diagnostic challenges.[] Hyperkinetic and hypokinetic movement disorders, including chorea, athetosis, dystonia, tremor, parkinsonism, and various mixed phenomenologies, have all been described in association with SSPE.[] In some patients, these manifestations may overshadow the characteristic myoclonic jerks and mimic primary movement disorders, autoimmune encephalitis, or neurodegenerative diseases, resulting in delayed diagnosis.[,] A 9-year-old boy was referred to the pediatric neurology clinic because of progressively worsening gait instability and involuntary movements that had developed over several months. According to his parents, he initially exhibited unsteadiness while walking, difficulty in changing direction, and intermittent truncal swaying. Over the following weeks, the involuntary movements became increasingly prominent, interfering with daily activities and leading to a marked decline in school performance. Clinical evaluation revealed progressive cognitive deterioration and behavioral changes accompanied by frequent involuntary movements. The patient experienced recurrent, sudden, brief, stereotyped myoclonic jerks predominantly involving the upper extremities and trunk. These episodes occurred multiple times throughout the day and occasionally disrupted gait and routine activities. His medical history was unremarkable, with no prior neurological illness. Vaccinations had been administered according to the National Immunization Schedule. Neurological examination demonstrated marked axial instability. The patient had difficulty in maintaining postural control while standing and exhibited a broad-based, unsteady gait. Frequent brief myoclonic jerks involving the trunk and upper limbs were observed [Video 1]. In addition, intermittent dystonic posturing of the upper extremities was noted. Irregular, flowing, and twisting choreoathetoid movements became particularly evident during voluntary actions. These movements varied in amplitude and occasionally spread from distal to proximal muscle groups. Given the predominance of hyperkinetic movement abnormalities, the initial diagnostic considerations included a primary movement disorder, neurodegenerative disease, or autoimmune encephalitis. Nevertheless, the progressive clinical course and accompanying cognitive decline suggested an underlying diffuse central nervous system disorder. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was entirely normal, with no detectable cortical, subcortical, white matter, or basal ganglia abnormalities. In contrast, electroencephalography revealed stereotyped, bilaterally synchronous, high-amplitude generalized periodic complexes recurring at regular intervals over a diffusely slowed background rhythm [Figure 1]. These characteristic periodic discharges represented the classic electroencephalographic hallmark of SSPE and strongly supported the diagnosis. Subsequent evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated anti-measles antibody titers in both cerebrospinal fluid and serum, confirming the diagnosis. Although periodic myoclonus remains the most recognized manifestation of SSPE, movement disorders may emerge at various stages of the disease and occasionally become the predominant clinical feature.[] In a large clinical series, Prashanth et al.[] documented a wide spectrum of movement disorders in patients with SSPE, including dystonia, chorea, tremor, and parkinsonism. Importantly, the authors emphasized that these manifestations were not limited to advanced disease stages and could dominate the initial clinical presentation.[] Similarly, Jagtap et al.[] reported that dystonic and choreiform movements may occasionally be more prominent than myoclonus, thereby obscuring the diagnosis. More recently, a systematic review by Garg et al.[] highlighted the remarkable heterogeneity of movement disorder phenomenology in SSPE and underscored the importance of recognizing atypical presentations. The pathophysiological basis of movement disorders in SSPE remains incompletely understood. However, involvement of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and cortico-striatal networks is believed to play a central role.[] Neuropathological studies have demonstrated degeneration and inflammatory changes within basal ganglia circuits, which may contribute to the development of hyperkinetic movement disorders.[] Neuroimaging studies have further suggested that thalamic and basal ganglia dysfunction may underlie the emergence of dystonia, chorea, and other abnormal movements.[,] Nevertheless, structural neuroimaging findings may be entirely normal, particularly during the early stages of the disease.[] The absence of MRI abnormalities in our patient likely reflects microscopic pathological changes that remain below the detection threshold of conventional imaging techniques.[] A particularly noteworthy aspect of the present case was the striking predominance of movement disorder manifestations. Video analysis demonstrated severe axial instability, dystonic posturing, choreoathetoid movements, and frequent myoclonic jerks. At first glance, this phenomenology was more suggestive of a primary hyperkinetic movement disorder than an epileptic encephalopathy. However, the presence of characteristic periodic electroencephalogram (EEG) complexes together with positive measles serology established the diagnosis unequivocally. This observation highlights the crucial role of EEG in the evaluation of children presenting with progressive movement disorders and cognitive decline. In conclusion, this video case illustrates that SSPE is not merely an encephalitic disorder characterized by periodic myoclonus but may also present with a movement disorder-dominant phenotype. Normal brain MRI findings should not exclude the diagnosis. In children presenting with progressive choreoathetoid movements, dystonic posturing, axial instability, and cognitive deterioration, the identification of periodic generalized complexes on EEG should raise strong suspicion of SSPE. In the consent form, the patient provided permission for the use of his clinical information and imaging findings for publication purposes. The patient understands that his name and initials will not be published and that every effort will be made to protect his identity; however, complete anonymity cannot be guaranteed. All clinical information, interpretation, scientific content, and conclusions were independently reviewed and verified by the authors, who accept full responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of the manuscript. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the broader clinical spectrum of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), particularly focusing on cases where movement disorders dominate the clinical presentation, challenging diagnostic accuracy. The authors sought to emphasize the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of SSPE, especially in the context of normal brain MRI findings and the critical role of electroencephalography (EEG) in diagnosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a single case report of a 9-year-old boy presenting with progressive gait instability and involuntary movements, initially considered for primary movement disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, or autoimmune encephalitis. The patient underwent clinical evaluation, neurological examination, and electroencephalography (EEG), with MRI showing normal findings. The diagnosis of SSPE was confirmed by elevated anti-measles antibody titers in cerebrospinal fluid and serum.
analysis.methods: The patient was evaluated through clinical assessment, neurological examination, and EEG. MRI was performed to rule out structural abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The patient exhibited progressive cognitive deterioration, behavioral changes, and frequent involuntary movements, including myoclonic jerks and dystonic posturing. EEG revealed characteristic periodic discharges, and elevated anti-measles antibody titers confirmed the SSPE diagnosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of SSPE, particularly when movement disorders dominate the clinical picture. The authors emphasized the critical role of EEG in diagnosing SSPE, even in the absence of typical MRI findings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against excluding SSPE based on normal MRI results and underscore the necessity of considering SSPE in the differential diagnosis of progressive movement disorders and cognitive decline. The study also highlights the importance of EEG in diagnosing SSPE.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single case report design, which does not allow for generalization. However, the findings are supported by characteristic EEG findings and elevated measles-specific antibody titers, providing strong evidence for the diagnosis of SSPE.

analysis.summary_en: This case report highlights the importance of recognizing atypical presentations of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), particularly when movement disorders dominate the clinical picture. source_body_en: More recently, a systematic review by Garg et al.[] highlighted the remarkable heterogeneity of movement disorder phenomenology in SSPE and underscored the importance of recognizing atypical presentations. However, involvement of the basal ganglia, thalamus, and cortico-striatal networks is believed to play a central role.[] Neuropathological studies have demonstrated degeneration and inflammatory changes within basal ganglia circuits, which may contribute to the development of hyperkinetic movement disorders.[] Neuroimaging studies have further suggested that thalamic and basal ganglia dysfunction may underlie the emergence of dystonia, chorea, and other abnormal movements.[,] Nevertheless, structural neuroimaging findings may be entirely normal, particularly during the early stages of the disease.[] The absence of MRI abnormalities in our patient likely reflects microscopic pathological changes that remain below the detection threshold of conventional imaging techniques.[] A particularly noteworthy aspect of the present case was the striking predominance of movement disorder manifestations. In conclusion, this video case illustrates that SSPE is not merely an encephalitic disorder characterized by periodic myoclonus but may also present with a movement disorder-dominant phenotype. Dear Editor, Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent infection of the central nervous system by a mutated measles virus.[] The disease classically presents with cognitive decline, behavioral deterioration, progressive impairment of scholastic performance, and stereotyped periodic myoclonus.[,] However, accumulating evidence indicates that the clinical spectrum of SSPE is considerably broader than previously recogn...

title: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh in 2026: national surveillance trends, cumulative divisional burden, and historical vaccination context
abstract: Background Bangladesh experienced a major measles resurgence in 2026. We reassessed early outbreak indicators while distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden and historical vaccination measures. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) bulletins dated 2–30 April 2026, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. We reconstructed cumulative division-level counts from the 22 April bulletin and calculated population-standardized notification rates using the 2022 census. Official national measles-containing vaccine coverage for 2019, 2023 and 2024 provided historical context. Results By 30 April, DGHS reported 37,131 suspected and 5,028 confirmed cases, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. On 22 April, cumulative division-level totals were 27,164 suspected and 3,934 confirmed cases. Dhaka recorded 2,634 confirmed cases, or 5.957 per 100,000 population. Official national MCV1 and MCV2 coverage in 2024 was 86.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Earlier childhood MR1 division-level measurements were not contemporaneous with the outbreak and were not used for correlation testing. Conclusions The early outbreak showed substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity. Accurate interpretation requires matching reporting windows, strengthening age- and vaccination-status surveillance and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage.

title_zh: 2026 年 麻疹 在孟加拉国复苏:国家 麻疹 趋势、累积部门负担和历史 疫苗接种 背景
source_body_en: Background Bangladesh experienced a major measles resurgence in 2026. We reassessed early outbreak indicators while distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden and historical vaccination measures. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) bulletins dated 2–30 April 2026, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. We reconstructed cumulative division-level counts from the 22 April bulletin and calculated population-standardized notification rates using the 2022 census. Official national measles-containing vaccine coverage for 2019, 2023 and 2024 provided historical context. Results By 30 April, DGHS reported 37,131 suspected and 5,028 confirmed cases, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. On 22 April, cumulative division-level totals were 27,164 suspected and 3,934 confirmed cases. Dhaka recorded 2,634 confirmed cases, or 5.957 per 100,000 population. Official national MCV1 and MCV2 coverage in 2024 was 86.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Earlier childhood MR1 division-level measurements were not contemporaneous with the outbreak and were not used for correlation testing. Conclusions The early outbreak showed substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity. Accurate interpretation requires matching reporting windows, strengthening age- and vaccination-status surveillance and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage.
